title: A profile anchor the validator accepts and the renderer cannot resolve crashes lore agent context with an uncaught exit 1
description:
Found by the LCLI-642 adversarial review (2026-09-29, reviewer report F1), in code this session did not write but did make reachable from a required CI context. DEFECT: `validateAgentProfileReferences` accepts an anchored profile reference whose heading the PACK RENDERER cannot resolve, and the renderer then throws a plain `Error` -- not a `LoreError` -- which the CLI reports as `{"error_type":"uncaught"}` with exit 1 and ZERO bytes of stdout. MECHANISM: `src/core/agent-profile.ts`'s `headingSlugs` walks every mdast node (`walkMdast`), while `src/core/agent-context.ts`'s `regionForReference` scans only TOP-LEVEL headings (`tree.children.filter(child => child.type === "heading")`). A heading nested in a blockquote, a list item or a footnote is therefore visible to the validator and invisible to the renderer. A plain typo on a `member::id`-qualified reference triggers it too, because the validator deliberately skips qualified references entirely. REPRODUCED (four shapes, verified through the real CLI on identical fixture bytes): an anchor on a heading inside a blockquote; an anchor whose plain slug a blockquoted duplicate heading shifts (`# Overview` inside a quote steals the slug, moving the real `## Overview` to `overview-1`); an anchor on a heading inside a list item; and `sources = ["other-member::reference/big#no-such-heading"]`. Each makes `bun run lore agent context

--task ...` exit 1 with `validated heading disappeared: ` and an empty stdout, where the contract reserves exit 1 for "the command broke" (cli-contract §5.1) and `lore check --help` advertises only 0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN LCLI-642: LCLI-642's check now DECLINES such a profile (counted `unmeasurable`) instead of letting the throw escape into `lore check`, because `lore check` is a required CI context and exiting 1 with no report is worse than not measuring. That is a guard at the new call site, not a repair: `lore agent context` still exits 1 on the same profiles, and the validator still accepts an anchor the renderer cannot honour. The repair belongs where the two disagree, and it needs a ruling on which side is right -- whether a nested heading SHOULD be a valid anchor target (in which case `regionForReference` is the bug) or the validator should reject what the renderer cannot resolve (in which case `headingSlugs` is) -- because the answer changes the profile contract for every consuming repository.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A profile reference anchored on a heading nested in a blockquote or a list item resolves: `lore agent context` exits 0 and the compiled item's body is the anchored region (DEC-22 option A; the accepted record reads status accepted at opum-agent origin/main since 7be97e7).

Slug agreement with the validator: every anchor `headingSlugs` admits, nested headings included, resolves in the renderer, and a nested duplicate heading no longer shifts a top-level heading's slug out of reach (the LCLI-642 review's slug-shift shape).

An unresolvable anchor (the qualified-typo shape `other-member::reference/big#no-such-heading`) fails as a classifiable `LoreError` with an advertised exit code (validation/6), not an uncaught exit 1 with empty stdout.

Every region-extraction path in agent-context.ts that assumed top-level headings (regionForReference, partitionMarkdown, breadcrumbAt) handles nesting: a nested heading's region ends at the next heading at depth <= it in document order, and its breadcrumb names its nested ancestors.

A regression test covers the blockquote-nested, list-item-nested, slug-shift and qualified-typo shapes from the LCLI-642 review, with a pre-fix control run in the same invocation proving the fixture reproduces the defect; the CLI-level pre-fix measurement (uncaught exit 1, empty stdout) is recorded on this task.
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.

plan: 1. Reproduce pre-fix: nested-anchor profile fixtures through the real CLI for the blockquote, list-item, slug-shift and qualified-typo shapes; record the uncaught exit 1 with empty stdout.

2. Fix: one shared document-order heading+slug enumeration (same walk and slugger as `headingSlugs`) consumed by regionForReference, breadcrumbAt and partitionMarkdown; an unresolvable anchor throws LoreError validation/6.
3. Tests: regression with a vendored pre-fix control in the same invocation; update the LCLI-642 capacity F1 case (a nested anchor becomes measurable).
4. Gates: bun test and bun run lore check solo (no concurrent bun test); PR into dev; close the task in the delivering PR.
implementationNotes:
RULING RELAYED, AND ITS PREMISE MEASURED BEFORE ACCEPTING IT: opum-agent messaged 2026-09-29 that the operator answered DEC-22 first-party (relay R-2026-09-29-03) choosing option A -- nested headings (inside blockquotes and list items) ARE valid anchor targets, so the RENDERER (regionForReference, src/core/agent-context.ts) is the side to fix, not the validator -- plus the requirement that every region-extraction path handle nesting and that lore agent context stop crashing on such profiles. It is AGAINST the recommendation this session offered, which is recorded here because the recommendation was offered as an A/B and A is a legitimate answer.

IT IS NOT YET READABLE FIRST-PARTY, and that is the state a successor must check rather than inherit. Read just now by ref: opum-agent origin/dev .quest/planning.json carries DEC-22 with status "proposed", not accepted, at origin/dev = 625bc1f4. THE ACs NEED REWRITING FIRST, which is why opum-agent asked for them first rather than last: AC1 currently reads "The disagreement is settled by a recorded decision, not by choosing a side in code: either ...", and the decision has now chosen a side, so the criterion as written is satisfiable by pointing at DEC-22 while the work it was meant to gate -- the renderer fix -- goes undone. The rewritten set should require: regionForReference resolves a heading nested in a blockquote or a list item, the qualified-typo shape still fails as a classifiable LoreError with an advertised exit code rather than an uncaught exit 1, the regression covers both shapes from the LCLI-642 review and fails against the pre-fix build in the same invocation, and bun test plus bun run lore check exit 0. Not started here by instruction: LCLI-648 was to finish first, and this boundary hands it on.

PRE-FIX MEASURED (2026-09-29, branch fix/LCLI-647-nested-anchor-renderer off origin/dev): all four LCLI-642 review shapes reproduced through the real CLI (bun run src/cli.ts agent context

--task ...) on a minimal fixture at /tmp/lcli647-repro: blockquote-nested anchor -> exit 1, 0 bytes stdout, {"error_type":"uncaught","message":"validated heading disappeared: quoted-heading"}; list-item-nested -> same with listed-heading; slug-shift (reference/dup#overview-1, where a blockquoted # Overview takes 'overview') -> same with overview-1; qualified typo (other-member::reference/big#no-such-heading) -> same with no-such-heading. This is the control the regression will be measured against.

FIXED on fix/LCLI-647-nested-anchor-renderer: one shared heading enumeration (anchoredHeadings in agent-profile.ts) now backs both headingSlugs (validator) and regionForReference (renderer), so slugs cannot diverge; nested headings carry scopeEnd (nearest container's end) so a nested section stops at its container and stops parenting later top-level headings; an unresolvable anchor is now LoreError validation/6 with hint, not a plain Error. Tests: test/lcli647-nested-heading-anchors.test.ts (9 cases, incl. the vendored pre-fix control at test/fixtures/lcli647/region-for-reference.pre-change.mjs run in the same invocation, and a current-source check that the vendored file is not the current one); test/check-agent-profile-capacity.test.ts F1 case flipped to [measurable] plus a new [unmeasurable] qualified-typo case. MEASURED: mutant dropping scope-awareness reddens exactly 2 of 9 ([scope],[breadcrumb]); mutant taking both sides back to top-level-only reddens 7 of 9 (all but [classifiable] and the vendored-file check); in the capacity file, comparison-forced-false reddens 4 of 11, annotation-off 1 of 11. Gates (pinned runtime /tmp/bun142/bin, PATH first): bun test 4820 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip across 136 files; bun run lore check exit 0 (Agent profiles: 4 read, 0 over capacity). The unpinned local bun is 1.3.14 and reds test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts -- the documented LCLI-648 pin trap, green under the pin.
finalSummary: The renderer now resolves every heading the validator admits: `anchoredHeadings` (src/core/agent-profile.ts) is one heading enumeration and one slug sequence, read by both `headingSlugs` and `regionForReference`; nested headings carry their container node and its end, so a nested section stops at its container, cannot end with a dangling marker, and a breadcrumb keeps its enclosing section's ancestor (a qualified pop). An unresolvable anchor is a LoreError validation/6 with a remedy, never the uncaught exit 1 with empty stdout the defect shipped. Tests: 12 cases including the vendored pre-fix resolver run in the same invocation, the four LCLI-642 review shapes, and the two fix-verification shapes; mutation map measured (F1's defect 1 of 12, F2's 1, unqualified pop 2, scope-awareness dropped 3, both readers top-level-only 9). Verified pre-fix on the same fixture bytes (exit 1, 0 bytes stdout, 'validated heading disappeared') and post-fix (exit 0 with the anchored regions; the typo shape exit 6). Gates on the pinned runtime: bun test 4823 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip (4824 ran); bun run lore check exit 0. Delivered as opum-ai/lore-cli#418; the run validating the deliverable is 36559296520 on 241725c0. Two adversarial review rounds plus a confirmation pass; all findings resolved (F1 scope collision, F2 dangling marker, breadcrumb ancestor eviction, CHANGELOG entry, map/comment inaccuracies).
